newsitem.title: CHINA: China railways send 3.6 mln tonnes grain to south.
newsitem.headline: China railways send 3.6 mln tonnes grain to south.

text.p: China's Shenyang Railway Administration has transported 3.6 million tonnes of grain from reserves in northeastern China to southern regions, the Economic Information Daily said on Tuesday.

"The administration started to transport the first batch of state grain reserves last September and the third batch is still being transported," an administration official said by telephone from Shenyang.
The railway had transported 3.6 million tonnes by April 16, the newspaper said.
Since receiving the order to ship the third batch in early March, the administration had moved 1.25 million tonnes to the northeastern port of Dalian, the newspaper said.

The administration had designated about 300 trains to carry the grain from Shenyang to Chengdu, the capital of southwestern Sichuan province, to Shanghai and Jinan, the capital of eastern Shandong province, and to Dalian, it said.

China shipped two million tonnes of corn to its southern provinces in late 1996 and a further 1.5 million tonnes early this year. The third batch of 3.0 million tonnes was now being moved to ease shortages in the south and reduce overstocked warehouses in the north.

Northeastern Heilongjiang, China's major corn-producing province, had by mid-April purchased 15 million tonnes of grain from the 1996 harvest, the China Business Daily said. Of that, seven million tonnes of grain had been dried as the province has battled to save damp grain from rotting.
